TheLounge's own stylesheet, vendored so the test pages show the theme in the cascade it
actually sits in: base CSS first, theme second. Not shipped - package.json `files` keeps
test/ out of the npm tarball.

  thelounge-4.5.2.css          package/public/assets/index-sODcR3vw.css
  fa-solid-900-BUswJgRo.woff2  referenced by that file, relative path kept
  fa-solid-900-DOXgCApm.woff   same

Source      npm thelounge@4.5.2, MIT, github.com/thelounge/thelounge
Published   2026-07-12 (65 days old at review, past the 30-day soak)
Publisher   GitHub Actions OIDC with SLSA provenance; registry signatures verify
Checked     no @import and no external hosts - the only url() references are the two
            fonts above, so this file fetches nothing over the network

Note        the test pages are not offline: theme.css opens with an @import of
            fonts.googleapis.com for the seven display fonts the theme uses - six that
            $name-styles picks between, plus Major Mono Display for lower_mono(), which
            sets headings, the lobby/network names, #nick and the userlist group labels.
            Read offline, all of that falls back to plain monospace with no warning.
Reviewed    2026-09-16

Vendored rather than added as a devDependency: we need one stylesheet, not a 3.7 MB
package with 24 dependencies, and the upstream filename is content-hashed
(index-<hash>.css), so a node_modules path would break on every release.

To refresh, re-run the review above and then:

  npm pack thelounge@<version>
  tar xzf thelounge-<version>.tgz
  cp package/public/assets/index-*.css test/vendor/thelounge-<version>.css
  cp package/public/assets/fa-solid-*.woff* test/vendor/

Then update the <link> in test/sample-channel.html and test/nicks.html, and delete the
old css. Check the fonts' hashed names too - they change independently.
